comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On dak.gg/er the PAM ad popup (whose blocked creative leaves the reporter's empty "광고 이미지" placeholder), the unfilled in-page ad slot #⁠er_top and the app-install bottom sheet were all reproduced in the AdGuard CLI baseline, and one domain-scoped cosmetic rule hiding exactly those three containers was verified (popup/slot/sheet visible in phase B, hidden in phase C, page integrity intact). Proposed for BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt. ## Rule `dak.gg##div:has(> div > #er_top),body > div[data-pam-popup],body > div:has(> div a.install-link[href*="gg.dak.bser"])` ## Policy rationale No rule of the run instruction's policy closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not a German (or any) anti-adblock wall - no detector request appears in the captured network log and the page shows no wall - and not a scam, phishing or tech-support page. The 'site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing' rule does not cover the reported ad containers:⁠ the popup carries a third-party advertiser creative (Monster Hunter Now) served through pam.dakgg.io / pam-assets.dak.gg and #⁠er_top is a Google ad slot left unfilled after the gpt tag is redirected, which is not self-promotion as the filter policy's Terminology defines it (goods or services owned by the site owner with no third-party compensation). The app-install bottom sheet is a self-promotion annoyance in the AdGuard Mobile App Banners category, which the repository already maintains rules for on this very site, so removing it is rule generation in the annoyance family rather than deliberate blocking of the site's own ads in the ad filters. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1b236f4815f33f6723f7b35a62e430ea41c310fc/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 1303](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1b236f4815f33f6723f7b35a62e430ea41c310fc/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L1303). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40799410252 Automated analysis against filters at `1b236f4`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

`goflix.sbs#%#//scriptlet('prevent-window-open')`

BaseFilter/sections/general_extensions.txt

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://adguard.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fadguard.com%2F) ### Comment > Subject: AdGuard for Windows UI fails to open / launch after hardware changes > > Hello AdGuard Support Team, > > I am experiencing a critical issue where the AdGuard for Windows user interface (GUI) completely refuses to open or launch. Despite multiple troubleshooting steps and clean reinstalls, the app window never appears on the screen. > > Here is the full background and a detailed list of everything that has been done so far: > > ### Hardware Context & Trigger: > 1. The issue started right after I performed major hardware changes: I replaced my GeForce GTX 970 with an RTX 4090 and reset my BIOS. > 2. Due to separate system/memory issues with the new card, I physically removed the RTX 4090 and reinstalled my original GTX 970. > 3. Since reverting back to the GTX 970, the AdGuard UI has completely disappeared and fails to load. > > ### Troubleshooting Steps Already Taken: > * Service Verification: I checked Windows Services (services.msc). The AdGuard Service is registered, status is Running, and it is set to Automatic. The background filtering engine seems to be working, but the GUI doesn't trigger. > * Direct Execution Commands: I attempted to force-launch the interface via the Windows Run dialog using "C:\Program Files\AdGuard\AdGuard.exe" /show as well as /show /reset. The command executes without any Windows error popup, but absolutely nothing happens on screen. > * Compatibility & Admin Mode: I applied "Run as Administrator" and tested running the executable in Windows 8 Compatibility Mode, with no success. > * Official Cleanup & Reinstallation: I downloaded and used the official AdGuard Uninstall Utility to perform a Standard Uninstall without deleting my user settings. After restarting the PC, I downloaded the latest installer from the official website and reinstalled it. The installer finished successfully, but the UI still won't open. > * GPU Hardware Acceleration Test: Suspecting a display conflict, I tried executing the command with the GPU bypass flag: "C:\Program Files\AdGuard\AdGuard.exe" /disable-gpu, but the interface still failed to render. > * Graphics Drivers Cleanup: I performed a completely clean installation of the official NVIDIA graphics drivers for the GTX 970 using the "Perform a clean installation" option to wipe any leftover registry paths or driver traces from the RTX 4090. The drivers were successfully updated, yet the issue persists. > * Antivirus Exclusion: I temporarily disabled my Avast Antivirus shields to ensure it wasn't silently blocking the UI thread from launching, which made no difference. > > ### Current State: > Fortunately, I have a safe manual backup of my %ProgramData%\Adguard folder (including the Backups directory with my .zip configuration files) saved on my desktop, so my data is secured. > > However, since the WPF/XAML graphical interface entirely fails to load, I cannot access my settings, check my license, or interact with the app. > > Given that the background service is running but the GUI is completely unresponsive (likely due to a deep rendering hook conflict caused by the GPU swapping/BIOS reset), could you please advise on how to force the UI to initialize or debug this specific crash? > > Thank you in advance for your assistance! ### Screenshots

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"44d93dbcb4f3aae61755dca9a089097919e799d783f2d8dc6f31f19c24fbb48f"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The Vietnamese anti-adblock wall (div.MuiDialog-root.block-ad-modal, "Vui lòng tắt tiện ích chặn quảng cáo để xem phim") appears only while filtering is active and is gone in an unfiltered control, but no detector script can be named from the captured requests, so per the anti-adblock policy the report goes to a maintainer. The narrow fix danet.vn#⁠#⁠.block-ad-modal hides the wall and its backdrop in the bound experiment, yet the vision review kept reading the site's own dark theme as a leftover overlay and hiding alone leaves MUI's body scroll lock, so it stays unverified.

## Still visible after the rule

- VUA ĐẦU BẾP MỸ - MÙA 8 / Danh sách tập | 21 tập / Thông báo — The whole movie-page area (title, description, episode thumbnails, related-film section) is covered by a dark dimming overlay and the content is withheld behind the anti-adblock "Thông báo" gate, so the episode list cannot be browsed; the dialog box itself is not legible in this tile, but the dimmed backdrop and the gated page content are visible.
- Full-page dim overlay covering the movie title/description, the "Danh sách tập | 21 tập" episode list, and the "Phim đề xuất" section; the centered dialog area itself is in the middle of this dimmed region — The entire movie page is visibly darkened by the anti-adblock modal's dimming backdrop:⁠ text, poster and episode thumbnails are all muted under a dark layer. The centered "Thông báo" dialog with the green "Tải lại trang" button is not rendered visibly in this capture, but its dimming overlay persists over the content the reporter could not reach, so the reporter-defined symptom footprint (overlay/modal region blocking the page) is still present.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ 'Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer.' The wall here is Vietnamese (not German), so the German-wall close rule does not apply; the detector is not a nameable request. Captured requests (artifact:⁠har:⁠9c3d645a-79b5-48f7-b2b1-6aaab37454d2 reporter profile, artifact:⁠har:⁠6cfdc49e-1973-49b4-ae50-d72ac55767a6 unfiltered control) contain no distinct detector script:⁠ everything is first-party danet.vn Next.js chunks plus the site's own ad loader /ads/adframe.js and /api/ads?type=OPENING_POPUP_BANNER_PROGRAMMATIC, so the blocker check cannot be attributed to a specific script from the inventory. The only cosmetic candidate (danet.vn#⁠#⁠.block-ad-modal) was not verified:⁠ the bound vision review returned 'not_resolved' in both of its completed runs, reading the page's own dark theme as a persistent dimming overlay, which the phase-B/phase-C DOM checks contradict; and hiding alone leaves MUI's inline body scroll lock (body style='overflow:⁠ hidden;') in place, so a companion rule is needed - a single-rule outcome cannot cover it.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/40815054569

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's cookie notice on www⁠.rescana.com is the site's own fixed bottom cookie bar (#⁠rescana-consent-banner), and no existing list rule touches it. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule, rescana.com#⁠#⁠#⁠rescana-consent-banner, was verified in the prepared AdGuard Browser Extension:⁠ the bar is visible before and gone after, with page integrity intact and no layout residue. ## Rule `rescana.com###rescana-consent-banner` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to block; it is not first-party advertising, not a paywall and not a German anti-adblock wall, so no run-instruction rule closes it. No rule in the repository covers www⁠.rescana.com (search_rules returns 0 matches for the domain, the selector and the script URL), so a new domain-scoped rule is needed. The fix is a cosmetic hide of the site's own consent bar, which the filter policy explicitly allows ('simply hiding ... the corresponding scripts is sufficient'). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d700b2d77a9c51532a209322139487bc88ee0644/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"af4764b87c9f2e0fc76360d281715296bdc817d9c9fde8aa8245e2fbb7814cfc"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

Reproduced the reporter's overlay live on the wiwo.de article:⁠ a German modal stating that an active ad blocker is presumably blocking the consent banner and asking the user to deactivate the blocker for the site and reload. That is a German site's anti-adblock wall, which the run instruction's filter policy excludes from rule generation ("no rule; recommend closing"), so the report is recommended for closing rather than patched.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "German anti-adblock walls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing. This covers only a German site's wall or popup that detects the ad blocker and asks to disable it or to allowlist the site. A page in German is not enough, and the reporter's choice of 'anti-adblock' as the problem type is not evidence:⁠ check what the page itself shows." The page itself shows the qualifying wall:⁠ the live and reported overlay reads "Das liegt vermutlich an einem aktiven Content- oder Adblocker, der unser Consent-Banner blockiert. Bitte deaktivieren Sie den Blocker für diese Website und laden Sie die Seite neu, um fortzufahren." with a "Seite neu laden" button, i.e. it detects the ad blocker and asks to disable it for the site. wiwo.de is a German site (html lang="de", German-language WirtschaftsWoche article), so the German-wall clause applies rather than the general anti-adblock clause. Run instruction:⁠ "The agent never closes an issue. 'Recommend closing' below means the report says no rule is needed; a maintainer checks it and decides." — this outcome recommends closing; the decision stays with a maintainer.

## Artifacts

`freetv.com##.install-android`

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported defect is the bottom-fixed cookie-consent bar (`div.l-cookie`) on www⁠.catchsecu.com, and a shared multi-domain rule for that exact selector already exists in the Cookies filter, so the fix is to add catchsecu.com to it. The candidate `catchsecu.com##.l-cookie` was validated in the AdGuard CLI filtering baseline:⁠ banner visible before, hidden after, page integrity intact, no remaining instances. ## Rule `catchsecu.com##.l-cookie` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules cover the site's own first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, and non-anti-adblock scams; none applies to a cookie-consent notice bar. The report is an annoyance (cookie notice), the kind the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to handle, so rule generation is open. Maintainer guidance in the instruction says to extend an existing shared rule when the fix fits it; the `.l-cookie` rule is that shared rule, so the host merges this domain-scoped candidate into it. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/511905dd1b122a347ccdaa6e78c4b18c0c968f03/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 11482](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/511905dd1b122a347ccdaa6e78c4b18c0c968f03/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L11482). ## Screenshots
